page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.8xlarge is a high clock speed virtual instance operating under the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are coupled with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. This instance configuration does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistence. Network connectivity operates with a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, and no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.hfg7.8xlarge consistently within the middle 50% average across standard tests. In raw compute tests, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1332.0 and a multi-core score of 11417.0, along with a PassMark CPU score of 31330.51. The processor incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, which aid numerical calculations and extended instruction workloads. System memory throughput measures 111.56 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 52.56 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while cached small-block reads reach 1856.24 GB/sec.

Workload tests show the instance handling Redis SET operations at 30.49 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 21.23 GB/sec. Given its balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio paired with high base clock frequencies, the ecs.hfg7.8xlarge is suited for compilation pipelines, enterprise web services, relational database instances, and distributed caching systems. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete reliance on external block storage, which shifts I/O latency dependencies entirely to network-attached storage infrastructure rather than direct-attached solid-state drives.
